subject: Region data lifecycle & expunge clarifications
messages:

Cc: Skyline Health Security <security@skylinehealth.com>

Subject: Question: hosted API - retention, backups and full expunge timeline

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the outreach yesterday. As part of our security review we need a succinct explanation of how Redwood handles data lifecycle for the hosted API. Our legal team has two specific asks:

1) If a customer requests complete deletion of tenant data, what is the end-to-end timeline (active stores, caches, snapshots, backups, and logs)?
2) How do you ensure deletion propagates to geo-replicated artifacts (snapshots / cross-region buckets)?
3) Do you offer proof-of-deletion or an attestation package we can retain?
4) Are there any common exceptions (legal hold, support escalations) that extend retention?

Can you respond with concrete timelines and the evidence package you can provide? Attachments are fine.

Best,
Samantha
Security Operations
Skyline Health

--
Note: We will also need a copy of any DPA language covering retention and destruction for our procurement team.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: hosted API - retention, backups and full expunge timeline

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, factual reply you can share with legal/procurement. I attached our retention matrix and a short "expunge playbook" summary for operational detail.

High-level answer (short version):
- Active stores & caches: user-submitted payloads (inputs/requests) are removed from the active serving layer within 0-24 hours of a verified deletion request. KV caches and ephemeral session caches obey configured TTLs (default: 1 hour) and we purge relevant prefixes immediately on request.
- Warm storage / tenant indexes: soft-delete is applied immediately; permanent purge from warm stores occurs within 30 days by default (this window allows rollback for accidental deletes).
- Backups & snapshots: backups are taken nightly; we maintain a rolling backup window of 90 days. For deletion requests, we remove the tenant from subsequent incremental backups and schedule cryptographic key rotation and snapshot pruning; full removal from backup artifacts is completed no later than 180 days. Where regulatory constraints require shorter windows we support contractual adjustments.
- Geo-replicated artifacts: replication is asynchronous. Deletion requests trigger a cascade that removes active copies and schedules snapshot pruning/replication tombstones. Cross-region copies are typically pruned on the next snapshot cycle; the full cascade is complete within the same timelines above (30d warm store / 180d backups).
- Logs & audit trails: operational logs that contain PII are redacted when possible; structured audit logs are retained for 1 year by default for troubleshooting and compliance, with the option to increase retention for customers that request longer windows.
- Proof & attestation: we provide a deletion attestation package (PDF) that includes timestamps for the request, confirmation of steps taken (active purge, soft-delete, snapshot pruning requests), and the IDs of the internal runbooks used. Evidence delivery typically occurs within 5 business days of completion.

Exceptions / holds:
- Legal or regulatory hold: deletion requests are suspended while a legally mandated hold is in place; we will notify the requester and provide support to Skyline's legal team.
- Disaster recovery / incident response: in rare cases (ongoing incident with recovery needs) retention may be extended temporarily; we document and notify customers.

Operational controls we use (summary):
- KMS-backed encryption per-tenant keys; cryptographic erasure for long-term backups where applicable.
- Snapshot tagging and tenant-aware backup indexes to allow targeted prune operations.
- Immutable audit trail of deletion requests and runbook executions stored under customer-specific IDs.

Attachments: data_retention_matrix.pdf (matrix + timeline), expunge_playbook_summary.pdf (runbook steps and evidence artifacts).

If you want, Ben (copied) can propose a short DPA addendum that shortens the backup window for Skyline; Jordan can arrange evidence/demo of the attestation package.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
